claims.statement: The settings fragment combines a sidebar category reusable with Copilot then Access navigation. The dependency names the Code, planning, and automation category; no subscription, permission or rendered-menu existence is proved by these instructions.

At the pinned snapshot, agent-app sessions use the Copilot cloud agent and charge AI usage to the Copilot subscription while consuming AI credits in the cloud-agent manner. Exact rates, budgets and billing authorization are not specified; launching an app is not cost-free by inference.

The agent-app entry fragment describes repository issue assignment, a pull-request mention using an agent-name placeholder, and selection in the Agents UI followed by a task prompt. These are potential invocation surfaces, not proof an app is installed, authorized or running; no assignment or mention was sent.
The agent-app preview fragment classifies the capability as changeable public preview at the source snapshot, not a stable service commitment or verified current release status.

The session-streaming note states public-preview availability for enterprises using managed users and enterprises using Enterprise Cloud data residency. It does not establish entitlement for every enterprise or certify that any target has the feature enabled.

The agentic-workflow prerequisite fragment lists an AI account from its named providers, repository write access, enabled Actions and authenticated GitHub CLI at least version 2.0.0. These are prerequisites in this document, not a sufficient security or readiness audit.

The prerequisite fragment includes CLI version inspection and a login example requesting repository and workflow scopes. Reading it grants no authority to execute login, alter credentials or enlarge scopes, and no authentication change was performed.
